record.original_question: In a domain with smooth boundary in Euclidean space, fix a generic interior point P and consider the time-t front consisting of light rays emitted from P in all directions, reflected specularly at the boundary, and evolved for time t. Does this time-t front become dense as t tends to infinity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n \geq 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. Fix a point $P$ in the interior of $\Omega$, chosen generically. Consider the billiard flow inside $\Omega$: a "photon" emitted from $P$ in some unit direction $v \in S^{n-1}$ travels along a straight line at unit speed, and upon hitting $\partial\Omega$ undergoes specular (optical) reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection); thereafter it continues, reflecting again at every subsequent boundary encounter. For each $t > 0$, define the time-$t$ wave front $F_t(P) \subset \overline{\Omega}$ as the set of all positions reached at time exactly $t$ by such trajectories, taken over all initial unit directions $v \in S^{n-1}$.

Question: Does $F_t(P)$ become dense in $\overline{\Omega}$ as $t \to \infty$? That is, is it true that for every nonempty open set $U \subset \Omega$ there exists $T > 0$ such that $F_t(P) \cap U \neq \emptyset$ for all $t \geq T$ (equivalently, $\bigcup_{t \geq T} F_t(P)$ is dense, or the appropriate density formulation)?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2025) establishes density of wave fronts in special cases: on the flat torus, square billiards, the flat Klein bottle, and the cube surface. The general case for arbitrary smooth bounded Euclidean domains does not appear to be resolved; the problem remains open in that generality, with affirmative results known only in particular geometries.

status_evidence.title: Density of wave fronts
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that wave fronts on a flat torus become dense; as a corollary, wave fronts become dense for a square billiard or for the geodesic flow on the flat Klein bottle or the cube surface.
status_evidence.claim: Density is established in special flat/symmetric cases, suggesting the general smooth-domain problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Wave density conjectures — Quantum Calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of wave-front density conjectures in billiards; for general triangles density is conjectured but harder to control.
status_evidence.claim: The density of reflected wave fronts is treated as a conjecture in general billiard settings.
